content:
[tab]        [ch]G[/ch]
Oh, the boll weevil is a little black bug, comes from Mexico they say.[/tab]

Came all the way to Texas, came a lookin’ for a place to stay.
[tab]                     [ch]D7[/ch]                         [ch]G[/ch]
came a lookin’ for a home, came a lookin’ for a home.[/tab]

[tab]         [ch]G[/ch]
Now, the first time I saw that little black bug, he was sittin’ up on a plant.  [/tab]

I said hey there boll weevil, if you think you’re gonna stay you can’t.
[tab]                   [ch]D7[/ch]                       [ch]G[/ch]
Go a lookin’ for a home, Go a lookin’ for a home.[/tab]

[tab]          [ch]G[/ch]
Well, the next thing I knew, that little black bug crawled around without a care.[/tab]

He was mighty well contented, ‘case he had his family there.
[tab]                   [ch]D7[/ch]                       [ch]G[/ch]
He was makin’ up a home, He was makin’ up a home.[/tab]

[tab]        [ch]G[/ch]
I got mad and told the little black bug, gonna spray you till y’all die, [/tab]

and the weevil said if you do it, my pals will come and multiply.
[tab]                       [ch]D7[/ch]                           [ch]G[/ch]
‘cause we gotta have a home, ‘cause we gotta have a home, [/tab]

[tab]     [ch]G[/ch]
So I got on my knees, Boll Weevil, said I, you’re a treatin’ me with scorn.  [/tab]

You done et up my cotton, and you’re startin’ in on my corn.
[tab]                       [ch]D7[/ch]                           [ch]G[/ch]
Can’t you find another home? Can’t you find another home?[/tab]

[tab]         [ch]G[/ch]
When the merchants came round to buy the cotton crop, I didn’t have a bale to sell.[/tab]

I couldn’t pay the mortgage, and heavily in debt I fell.
[tab]                    [ch]D7[/ch]                        [ch]G[/ch]
Now I haven’t got a home, Now I haven’t got a home, [/tab]
[tab]                    [ch]D7[/ch]                        [ch]G[/ch]                    [ch]G6[/ch]
Now I haven’t got a home, Now I haven’t got a home.[/tab]


Strum pattern: DDUUDU

There are many versions of this traditional folk song. I like this version because it tells the story 
clearly and cleverly. I've made some minor modifications to make it easier to sing the lyrics.
